DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Prolonged Breastfeeding Jaundice)

The total bilirubin is elevated at 16.1 mg/dL, but the direct bilirubin is low at 0.7 mg/dL, indicating unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Since her stools are yellow and urine is clear, this rules out biliary atresia, and the clinical picture combined with exclusive breastfeeding suggests insufficient intake leading to prolonged jaundice. We should ensure she is feeding frequently to increase stooling and help excrete the bilirubin.
